direct.system:
Execute list instructions exactly. A list has positions ordered from first to last; duplicate values occupy separate positions. Each operation replaces the current list. The next instruction uses that NEW list. Never reuse the initial list after a step.
Exact semantics (operation name: meaning):
reverse: read ALL entries from last to first, reversing their order. This is not sorting or rotation.
sort_asc: arrange ALL entries smallest to largest, preserving duplicates.
sort_desc: arrange ALL entries largest to smallest, preserving duplicates.
remove_first k: delete exactly positions 1 through k; keep everything AFTER position k. k is a count, not a value.
keep_first k: keep exactly positions 1 through k and discard the rest.
remove_all x: delete EVERY entry whose VALUE equals x. Keep other entries in their existing order.
add k: add k to EVERY value, keeping positions and length unchanged.
multiply k: multiply EVERY value by k, keeping positions and length unchanged.
keep_even: keep values divisible by 2, including 0; remove odd values. Preserve order.
keep_odd: keep values not divisible by 2; remove even values including 0. Preserve order.
rotate_left k: split AFTER the first k entries into prefix and suffix; output the entire suffix followed by the entire prefix. Preserve order INSIDE each part. All entries appear once.
swap_ends: exchange ONLY the first and last entries; every middle entry stays in its place. Length zero or one is unchanged.
append x: attach ONE copy of x after the last entry; all previous entries stay unchanged.
unique: scan left to right, keeping the first occurrence of each value; discard later occurrences without sorting.
